jobs.location_raw: Remote, U.S, Ann Arbor, MI, Fort Worth, TX, Blacksburg, VA
jobs.description_text: Meet the team Torc’s Perception teams develop the production machine learning systems that enable our autonomous trucks to understand their surroundings. The Active Sensors team owns the end-to-end lidar perception pipeline, from motion compensation and point-cloud aggregation to multitask learned perception for object detection, road and lane understanding, 3D occupancy estimation for safe vehicle operations. These systems must run in real-time on embedded compute while remaining robust to adverse weather, sensor degradation, and sensor failures. The team works across machine learning, 3D perception, and embedded systems, balancing perception performance and robustness against latency, memory, power and on-board compute budget. As the team’s Engineering Manager, you will lead development across the complete perception lifecycle, from data requirements and pipeline architecture through model training, evaluation, integration, deployment, and robotic testing. You will collaborate closely with teams across sensor hardware, data, infrastructure, simulation, compute platform, systems engineering, safety, perception, and planning. What you'll do: The Perception department is seeking an experienced and technically strong Engineering Manager to lead a machine learning team developing active sensor-based perception capabilities for our autonomous trucks. jobs.description_text: Meet the Team The System Triage team plays a critical role in understanding how Torc's autonomous driving software performs in the real world. Through analysis of vehicle data, system performance indicators, and software quality metrics, the team helps engineering leaders identify trends, investigate complex system behaviors, and make informed decisions as we advance toward production. Within System Triage, the Metrics & Analysis team focuses on turning large volumes of autonomous vehicle data into meaningful engineering insights. From evaluating system performance and traffic law compliance to developing metrics, dashboards, and analysis tools, the team provides visibility into the performance and maturity of our autonomous driving technology. As the Engineering Manager for Metrics & Analysis, you'll lead a team of technical professionals, establish consistent analytical approaches, and help scale the tools and processes that support engineering decision-making. This is an opportunity to remain close to the technical work while shaping how the team operates, develops, and delivers insights across the organization. What you'll do: A successful candidate will have experience in people management, cross-functional collaboration, and hands-on data analysis to support system triage and software quality reporting. This role is fundamentally about partnership: working closely with one of the great cultural critics of our time to keep developing the show and reaching new heights; and leading a small team of producers to translate Wesley's critical voice, instincts, and curiosity into a show that feels as engaging as it is intellectually sharp. The show's format is loose and conversational. Episodes are built around Wesley's exchanges with fellow critics, artists, and cultural figures; at their best they feel real, incisive, intimate, surprising, loose, unpredictable and crackling with on-the-fly cultural criticism. The senior editor will play a key role in refining this format, ensuring that each episode feels cohesive, dynamic, and fun while showcasing the distinct voice and authority that define Wesley's work. This job is for you if: you are a rigorous editor, a strong producer and an active, generative collaborator — someone who can listen as well as direct. You enjoy the give and take involved in challenging, sharpening, and expanding ideas in real time with a dynamic team. You know and have respect for Wesley's critical voice. jobs.description_text: The New York Times is looking for a FOIA editor to oversee and guide our strategy of using the Freedom of Information Act and other local, state and federal public records laws to obtain information from governmental and public entities. You will serve as a hub for the newsroom’s public records requests, helping provide resources and guidance to journalists across The Times about how to maximize our ability to obtain information in the public’s interest. You will serve as a consultant to teams on effective tactics, working with reporters and editors at the inception of stories and projects to help integrate FOIA requests early in the process. You will also be responsible for developing story ideas and original coverage through the FOIA process, identifying opportunities to obtain public records that will generate news. You are excited to experiment with new technology and formats and collaborate with our data, visual and product teams to tell stories that resonate with our audience. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM Discovery is Anduril's team for the hard concepts: the ones that are not yet proven or built. We take the newest and hardest problems across space, missiles, air, sensors, autonomy, and cyber, decide what is worth building, and prove it out: we build the models, break the assumptions, run the tests, and carry what works to the point where a program can pick it up. We work with hardware and software engineering teams across the company, driving cross-functional collaboration across different business lines. ABOUT THE JOB We are building an expeditionary force: a small group of engineers who want to do big, new, hard things and who move into unfamiliar territory as a matter of course. As Deputy Chief Engineer in Discovery, you lead the technical work on concepts nobody has proven, usually several at once. You learn whatever domain each one lives in and build the thing that tests it: the prototype, the test article, the demonstration. Analysis gets a concept to the point where it is worth building; building it is how we find out. You are the technical authority for the concepts you own: you set the approach, review the work, and decide, on the evidence, which concepts continue and which stop. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM Discovery is Anduril's team for the hard concepts: the ones that are not yet proven or built. We work with hardware and software engineering teams across the company, driving cross-functional collaboration across different business lines. ABOUT THE JOB We are building an expeditionary force: a small group of engineers who want to do big, new, hard things and who move into unfamiliar territory as a matter of course. As a Discovery Engineer you pick up a concept nobody has proven, learn whatever domain it lives in, build the analysis or prototype that tests it, and get to an answer. The problems change; the approach does not: reason from first principles, do the work, check it, and reach a solution. You are not hired for a particular skill set. You are hired for a record of getting engaged in problems across different areas, being analytic, testing new concepts, and getting to solutions. You are also the adversary to our own ideas. Autonomy is only as good as the link that carries it. That is the problem you would own. ABOUT THE JOB We are seeing a Mission Autonomy Lead on the Thunder team at our Costa Mesa, CA office. In this role, you will own the Autonomy software stack within Mission Systems for a Thunder, owning the software that enables autonomous mission execution. Reporting to the Mission Systems Lead, you will cover system design, mission planning, mission operations, perception, debrief, and software development infrastructure. You will define how the vehicle plans, executes, perceives, and learns from missions autonomously across long ranges of open ocean beyond line of sight. Your spectrum of support will be diverse in nature and require you to leverage your technical expertise as well as leadership skills to set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and rapidly drive to completion. jobs.department: Maritime & Maneuver Dominance : Undersea Dominance - Engineering & Operations : Program & Product Management
jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM At Anduril, we are developing unmanned systems for subsurface, surface, land, and air domains that will leverage unsupervised autonomy for the delivery of multi-mission capability to our customers. Deciding what to build — and in what order — requires people who can connect operational problems, threat-informed scenarios, customer needs, and product employment concepts to the capability we field. We are looking for a Mission Operations Engineer to do that work at the enterprise level, based at our Costa Mesa, California headquarters. ABOUT THE JOB Our next Mission Operations Engineer has built and executed plans in the maritime domain, has stood watch, and has been to sea, preferably using uncrewed systems. That background is what separates an analytic product that operators recognize as real from one that reads well and gets ignored. Equally important is the ability to carry that work into a room of senior military and civilian decision-makers and hold it there: this role briefs Commanding Officers, high-level civilians, and our own executive team, and it is expected to give direct answers under hard questioning. Customer engagement is key, with opportunity to embed directly with our warfighters to provide real-time analysis and feedback on Anduril products. jobs.description_text: ABOUT THE TEAM Anduril is seeking a Mission Systems Lead to join the Omen team at our Costa Mesa HQ. Omen is Anduril’s hover-to-cruise autonomous air vehicle (AAV) that packs the endurance, payload, and mission flexibility of much larger airplanes into a novel runway-independent Group 3 platform. Omen can operate from ship decks, beaches, or remote island clearings, providing true runway independence and freedom of maneuver across defense and civilian domains. Omen is the first tail-sitter aircraft with a mass-production contract, with an order of 50 systems representing a decisive investment that anchors production and accelerates the development of future systems. You will work on new aircraft development in a lean, high-ownership culture where you directly shape the product and operate at a velocity to fly new designs within months, not years ABOUT THE JOB You will lead a technical team in the development and integration of Omen’s Mission Systems, from initial concept through delivery. This encompasses mission perception, mission autonomy, and payload systems.
